system:
You are a senior SOC analyst investigating Kubernetes activity. Work only from evidence returned by your tools; never invent event IDs, IPs or principals.

Scope: one day (2026-10-14) of Kubernetes API audit logs for the payments-prod cluster, which runs on AWS (EKS), GCP (GKE) and Azure (AKS).

Data: ocsf_api_activity holds all three clouds normalized to the OCSF API Activity schema (one row per audit event; metadata.uid is the audit event ID). Purpose-built tools search and summarize it and look up identity, IP, service-account, cluster and allowlist context; query_sql is available for anything else.

Method: start broad, form hypotheses, verify each against the data, and check enrichment context before concluding. Cite every malicious event you rely on by its audit event ID. When finished, call submit_verdict exactly once; the investigation ends when you do.

input.summary: This is malicious. Jordan Doe's (jdoe@example.com) credentials for all three clouds were used from 198.51.100.23, a bulletproof VPS in NL (NIGHTOWL-HOSTING) that threat feeds list as malicious, with an open Docker registry on port 5000. Jordan is on PTO 10-12..10-19 and normally uses macOS, but the client here was linux kubectl. The attacker ran the same playbook on EKS (14:02-14:25), GKE (14:38-15:01) and AKS (15:11-15:34). Each time they checked their permissions, listed namespaces, failed to read kube-system secrets or create a kube-system job, then read payments secrets including payments-db-credentials. Next they started a privileged hostPID pod with the host root mounted (debug-tools-7f9c, not on the allowlist) and exec'd nsenter into the node. They then used the cluster-admin argocd-application-controller service account token (most likely taken from the node), which is only supposed to be used in-cluster, from 198.51.100.23 to create ClusterRoleBinding 'jdoe-break-glass' giving jdoe cluster-admin. Finally they set up persistence: a kube-system DaemonSet 'kube-metrics-agent' and CronJob 'node-cert-rotate' that both pull images from 198.51.100.23:5000, plus NodePort service 'metrics-agent-np' on port 30080. They ended by listing secrets across all namespaces, which fired the alert. All three payments-prod clusters are fully compromised: assume every cluster secret is exposed and the argocd token is stolen.

It is not on the allowlist, but it matches the standard 'kubectl debug node' pattern: busybox image, pinned to a named node, from corp VPN IP 203.0.113.12, on her usual darwin client, with no follow-up activity. Likely benign; confirm with her.
external-secrets and cert-manager service accounts read *-db-credentials and *-tls secrets from in-cluster IPs on a steady schedule: normal controller behavior.
argocd-application-controller activity from its in-cluster IPs (10.0.12.173, 10.128.0.212, 10.224.0.158) is normal GitOps. Only its use from 198.51.100.23 is malicious.
Routine developer/SRE pods/exec and get pods/secrets from corp egress IPs 203.0.113.x in their own app namespaces.
Updates to system clusterrolebindings at 03:05 by eks:addon-manager, aksService and system:addon-manager are platform reconciliation.
